strategy.headline: Contrarian but not stupid: when an underdog is worth taking
strategy.summary: Contrarian is a risk choice, not a scoring bonus. Hotspawn awards points for correct picks by tier; this project has no verified Hotspawn user pick-share data, so a market underdog is not necessarily a crowd underdog. Default to the higher sourced win probability. If you intentionally accept variance for differentiation, limit the swings and require a concrete, sourced matchup, roster, schedule or form reason; this is a project heuristic, not a proven leaderboard edge.

rules.rule: Consider a roster-change angle only when the change is verified, recent and structural.
rules.why: A new IGL or multiple new starters can change roles and coordination, but roster change alone does not prove weakness. State the transfer date, player overlap and the results since the move. Aurora's July 2026 rebuild was about three months old by TWC, so it was not a fresh day-four onboarding explanation.
rules.verify: Use the team's announcement and a fixture-specific roster page; name the date and confirmed players rather than treating 'new roster' as a probability.

rules.rule: Use rest or travel only after comparing both teams' schedules.
rules.why: A favourite's short rest is relevant to an underdog only if the underdog has a better schedule. If the underdog also played later or more maps, rest is a counterweight, not an upset argument. A schedule difference is not a measured fatigue effect.
rules.verify: Compare each side's last match time and map load from the event schedule/results; do not infer fatigue or travel from a result alone.

sources.label: HLTV TWC 2026 event results and schedule

rules.rule: Treat the 15–40% underdog band as a risk screen, not an edge signal.
rules.why: A 15–40% market-implied win chance implies a 60–85% loss chance; that is not a calibrated guarantee, and Hotspawn gives no underdog bonus. It can differentiate only if fewer entries chose it; no crowd-share data is verified here. Treat any such selection as a deliberate high-variance swing, not a market-backed value pick.
rules.verify: Use the sourced market line and Hotspawn's scoring rules. Without verified pick-share data, do not claim the market underdog is unpopular or leaderboard-optimal; where no market exists, label the pick research-only with no percentage.

rules.rule: Never size up a contrarian pick on an identity or a number you cannot source.
rules.why: Renamed teams, academy squads and unclear aliases are exactly where a whole pick'em slips away on a wrong team.
rules.verify: Check the exact opponent pair and UTC start in the sourced identity register, then confirm the roster on a fixture-specific source.

rules.rule: Limit how many contrarian swings you take per slate.
rules.why: Multiple low-probability picks can compound missed points. The one-or-two-swing limit is a project risk-control heuristic, not a statistically optimized or proven leaderboard strategy.
rules.verify: Count the proposed swings, use the published tier points and probabilities, and label the limit as a heuristic; no verified crowd-share model is available.

sources.label: Official fixture feed with tier/point fields

rules.rule: Weight the swing by what the fixture is worth, and count the streak you would break.
rules.why: Hotspawn awards more points for higher tiers and a bonus for consecutive correct picks, so a contrarian miss costs the fixture's points plus the streak. In the current feed a tier-S match is worth 7 points, tier-B 3 and tier-C 2: a wrong tier-C swing costs 2 points, a wrong tier-S swing costs 7 and the bonus run with it.
rules.verify: Hotspawn's official how-it-works rules page, which the day-three points above link directly, plus the offered_points and points_breakdown fields in the fixture feed; expected points are then offered_points x the published probability, which is arithmetic on a sourced line, never a new probability.

sources.label: Official fixture feed with offered_points and points_breakdown

unverified: Hotspawn's scoring rules are now collected from the official rules page and from the fixture feed's offered_points field: points per correct pick, more points for higher tiers (7 / 3 / 2 for tiers S / B / C in the current feed), a bonus for consecutive correct picks, picks locking before start and a weekly leaderboard reset. What is still not verifiable from any source this project can read is the exact streak-bonus formula, so no number is claimed for it and no claim is made about how many extra points a correct underdog earns relative to a favourite beyond the tier weighting.

No verified Hotspawn user pick-share feed or calibrated historical leaderboard model is available in this project. A market underdog is not proof that entries favor the other side, and no leaderboard advantage is claimed; the published lines are market-implied estimates or explicitly labelled model lines, not a calibrated independent forecast.
